title: Lesson 1: The Great Commission - Your Personal Ministry
description: Four friends carried a man to Jesus, and Jesus saw their faith. This lesson opens Growing Out by showing that God grows your faith for the faith of others, and that your personal ministry begins with the names already in your life.

blocks.text: Welcome to Growing Out

The 200-level path has three connected courses. Growing Deep (201) was about loving God. Growing Up (202) was about loving the people God has placed beside you. Now in Growing Out (203), the branches begin to bear fruit, as that love reaches people who do not yet know Jesus.

blocks.alt: Growing Together Discipleship Series: Starting in Discipleship, Growing Out with the Gospel, and Leading in Discipleship

blocks.title: Four Friends and a Roof
blocks.text:
Jesus was teaching in a house in Capernaum, and the crowd was so thick that no one else could get near the door. Then four men arrived, carrying a paralyzed man on a mat. He could not walk to Jesus, and now his friends could not carry him through the crowd.

They did not turn around and go home. They climbed onto the roof, dug an opening through it, and lowered the man down on his mat until he lay right in front of Jesus.

What happened next begins with a surprising phrase: "And when Jesus saw their faith, he said to the paralytic, 'Son, your sins are forgiven'" (Mark 2:5). Then, so everyone would know He has authority to forgive sins, Jesus told the man to get up. He stood, picked up his mat, and walked out in front of them all. The whole crowd gave glory to God and said, "We never saw anything like this!" (Mark 2:12).

Read that phrase again: Jesus saw their faith. Mark does not give the four men's names, but they believed Jesus could help, and their faith went to work for a man who could not get there by himself. They could not heal him, and they could not forgive him. What they could do was carry him to the One who can.

That is the heart of this course. God grows your faith so He can work through you for the faith of others. Your personal ministry is loving the people God has placed in your life and helping them know and follow Jesus.
1.1 - Who is one person you would love to see come to know Jesus?
Think Beyond Your Tree

Most of what you have learned so far has been about your own growth: deeper roots, a stronger trunk, wider branches. Those are good gifts, and God is not finished growing you. But notice something about a fruit tree. It does not eat its own fruit. The fruit is for someone else, and inside the fruit is the seed of another tree.

The same is true of what God is growing in you. Your patience helps someone feel safe. Your generosity lifts someone's burden. Your words help someone understand the good news. So add a new question to your growth: Who is being helped by what God is growing in me? Think beyond your tree, and pray for the orchard.

This is not a way to earn anything. You are already a loved child of God, and a tree does not strain to make fruit. It stays rooted, and the fruit comes. Personal ministry is not a sales pitch or a quota. It is the overflow of a heart Jesus has rescued.
1.2 - Who is being helped by what God is growing in you, or who could be?
Jesus Sends Ordinary People

After Jesus rose from the dead, eleven disciples met Him on a mountain in Galilee. Not long before, every one of them had run away, and even now, "when they saw him they worshiped him, but some doubted" (Matthew 28:17). Jesus did not go looking for a better team. He gave these forgiven, unsure, ordinary men His mission.

And Jesus came and said to them, "All authority in heaven and on earth has been given to me. Go therefore and make disciples of all nations, baptizing them in the name of the Father and of the Son and of the Holy Spirit, teaching them to observe all that I have commanded you. And behold, I am with you always, to the end of the age."

This is called the Great Commission, and it is addressed to you too. Look at how it is wrapped. It opens with His authority and closes with His presence, and in between is one clear direction: go. Jesus does not tell His followers to wait and hope people come to them. He sends them. You do not have to be fearless or finished to be sent. You only have to belong to the One who sends you.
Love Has Names
So where do you go? Just before Jesus returned to the Father, He drew the map.
But you will receive power when the Holy Spirit has come upon you, and you will be my witnesses in Jerusalem and in all Judea and Samaria, and to the end of the earth.

Jesus started His followers in Jerusalem, the city where they already were. The mission reaches the whole world, and you will come back to that later in this course, but it begins with the people who already know you.

The four friends did not carry a crowd. They carried one man. Loving your neighbor becomes real when your neighbor has a name and a face: the people in your home, the people beside you at work or school, and the people in your neighborhood and everywhere else you keep showing up. Love has names.

One question sits underneath your map: Does everyone who knows me know the good news of Jesus? That is not asking whether you have preached at everyone. It is asking whether the people in your regular life have seen enough of your faith and heard enough of your story to know what you believe and why.
1.3 - Start your map here. Write two or three names for each circle: home, work and school, and your neighborhood.
You Carry, Jesus Heals

If this feels like a lot, go back to the roof. The four friends did not heal anyone. Their part was to bring their friend close to Jesus, and what happened next was His part. It is the same for you. You cannot change anyone's heart, and God does not ask you to. He asks you to love people and bring them near. His Spirit lives in you to give you words and open doors, and the results belong to Him. Your part is to carry. His part is to heal.

You will not have to guess how. In the next four lessons, you will learn the BLESS rhythms, a simple way to love the people on your map: Begin with prayer, Listen, Eat, Serve, and Story. Share your life, and share the good news.
1.4 - How would you explain your personal ministry to a friend in one minute?
This Week's Practice

Choose one name from your map, the person God is placing on your heart, and pray for them by name each day this week. It took four friends to carry one man, so tell one Christian friend the name you chose and ask them to pray with you.
Lesson 1 Review

Four friends carried a man to Jesus, and Jesus saw their faith. God grows your faith so He can work through you for the faith of others. That is your personal ministry: loving the people God has placed in your life and helping them know and follow Jesus. He sends ordinary, unfinished people with His authority and His presence, and He starts them with the people they already know. Think beyond your tree, pray for the orchard, and remember that love has names.
In the next lesson, you will begin the BLESS rhythms where every one of them starts, with prayer for the names on your map.
Closing Reflections
What is one key thing you learned from this lesson?
What is one step you are going to take this week?
What is a prayer request for this week?
